sections.content:
The red chevron in the upper left only moved the 5 blocks in the top row: S(6,17)→b, b(6,23)→g, g(6,29)→p, p(6,35)→w, w(6,41)→S. In other words, the top row (6,17),(6,23),(6,29),(6,35),(6,41) is a 5-cycle that moves to the right (each block moves to the next column position, and S wraps around from (6,41) back to (6,17)).
Wait: (6,17) became b (old (6,23)), (6,23) became g (old (6,29)), (6,29) became p (old (6,35)), (6,35) became w (old (6,41)), (6,41) became S (old (6,17)). So the cycle: (6,17)→(6,23)→(6,29)→(6,35)→(6,41)→(6,17). A 5-cell ring! The red chevron rotates this ring in the direction of (6,17)→(6,41) (rightward), i.e., each block moves to the next cell to the right, wrapping around.
So the chevron rotates a small ring. The Y 2x2 ring around S(6,17) is... hmm, but the Y ring didn't move. Interesting — the Y 2x2s at (4,15),(4,21),(10,15),(10,21) didn't change. So they're static decoration? Or part of a different cycle controlled by a different chevron.
Wait, but the S block moved from (6,17) to (6,41) — the Y ring stayed around the old position. So the Y ring is static (decoration/target marker?). Hmm, or the Y ring is part of a vertical cycle controlled by the middle-left red chevron (34,9)?
Let me try clicking the middle-left red chevron (37,11) to check its cycle.

<function=python>
<parameter=code>
def snap(fr):
    d = {}
    for n in fr.segmentation['nodes']:
        if n['pixels'] in (4,16,8):
            b=n['boundary']; r0=min(p[0] for p in b); c0=min(p[1] for p in b)
            d[(r0,c0)]=n['color']
    return d
res = action([{'action':'MOUSE','row':37,'col':11}])
before = snap(last_transition.before_frame); after = snap(current_frame)
diff = [(k,before.get(k),after.get(k)) for k in sorted(set(before)|set(after)) if before.get(k)!=after.get(k)]
print(len(diff),"changed")
for k,a,b in diff: print(k,a,'->',b)
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
